To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the autotransplanation of spontaneous tumours from old mice to young hosts results in tumour growth, but the latency period is prolonged.
spontaneous tumours in aged mice are resistant to autochton transplantation.
the autotransplantaion method can be used to detect antitumour resistance in spontaneous tumours, but it is less sensitive than the transplantation-excision- retransplantation method.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question, whether the resistance of the host against tumour growth can be detected and measured in the case of spontaneous tumours.
the development of a method which allows to study spontaneous antitumour resistance of the mouse.

the question whether the spontaneous tumours of Balb/c mice are able to induce an antitumour resistance in the host, and whether the autotransplanted tumour cells can be used as an assay to detect such a resistance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the spontaneous Balb/c tumour is a tumour which can be used for antitumour screening in the mouse but that the method is not as sensitive as the transplantation-excision-reatransplantation assay using the benzpyrene induced fibrosarcoma.
spontaneous tumours of mice are capable of inducing resistance against their autologous cells.
the autotransplation method is not an adequate method for detection of antitumoral resistance against spontaneous tumours.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the spontaneous tumours of aged mice have the ability to develop into recidives and/or metastases, although the antitumour resistance of the host is not always effective in preventing the growth of the tumour cells.
in the Balb/c mouse the antitumour immunity is not able to prevent the growth of spontaneous tumours, but it may be effective in preventing the growth of tumour cells in a state of low cellularity.
in the course of the experiments the antitumour effect of the autochtonal host was not demonstrated.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the autotransplanation method can be used for detection of antitumoral resistance in the case of spontaneous tumours, although the results obtained with this method have to be confirmed by other techniques.
the autotransplanation method is not a reliable tool to detect the presence of antitumor immune response.
the auto-transplantation method is not a suitable tool for the detection of antitumoral resistance.
